title: Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with Large Language Models

mechanism.domainTask: Automated discovery of CFR and PSRO algorithms for imperfect-information games
mechanism.populationDetail: The outer search maintains one unpartitioned population P of baseline and valid evolved algorithm programs.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate best-so-far or elite archive is described for the outer search.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The discovered PSRO solver also maintains policy populations, but those are inside evaluated candidates and are not the evolutionary search population.
mechanism.generationDetail: One selected current program is changed through SEARCH/REPLACE patches whose search chunks are limited to four lines; multiple patches may alter algorithmic behavior broadly.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Per-game negative exploitability and their average are the defined fitness objectives; one objective is sampled for fitness-biased parent selection.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: A fitness objective is randomly selected when multiple per-game and aggregate scores exist; sampling then favors high values on that objective.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The object evolved is a game-learning algorithm; one discovered PSRO algorithm has its own policy population and exploration schedule, distinct from the outer evolutionary search.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Discovering Multiagent Learning Algorithms with Large Language Models.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Current survey cites this paper only under applications. Outer AlphaEvolve search supports additional mechanism placements. Do not classify SHOR-PSRO's scheduled internal policy as outer search control; archive and reference retrieval rules are unspecified.
